eligibility.quote: The `ros2 topic echo` seems to cause unlimited memory consumption and makes the system run OOM in a matter of seconds.

failed_conditions.quote: That matches what we have in the rmw/types.h define. Also update the tests to conform.
The crash is triggered by an invalid (excessively large) size argument passed to `resize`.

loudness.quote: ==139==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: allocator is out of memory trying to allocate 0x16f6337da8 bytes

resolution.quote: I've just tested backporting this to Humble, compiling locally and indeed this fixes the issue reported in https://github.com/ros2/rmw_fastrtps/issues/797

notes: Independently verified. #797 body: docker-compose with `image: ros:jazzy` / `command: "ros2 topic list"` and `image: ros:humble` / `command: "ros2 topic echo /chatter std_msgs/String"`, same ROS_DOMAIN_ID; the OOM quote is verbatim; reporter also notes "we do see the error output caught in https://github.com/ros2/rmw_fastrtps/pull/737 on the humble node" and that rmw_cyclone_cpp does not crash — confirming this is a rmw_fastrtps_cpp behaviour. #828: I read "[ros2run]: Killed", the ASAN stack (std::vector<rmw_dds_common::msg::Gid_<...> >::resize(unsigned long) called from rmw_dds_common::msg::typesupport_fastrtps_cpp::cdr_deserialize(... NodeEntitiesInfo_<...>&) via ParticipantEntitiesInfo cdr_deserialize and _ParticipantEntitiesInfo__cdr_deserialize), the mechanism quote "The crash is triggered by an invalid (excessively large) size argument passed to `resize`." (reader_gid_seq.resize marked "// <-- crash*"), and the bad_alloc handler text "'Bad alloc' exception deserializing message of type %s.". rmw_dds_common PR #68 title is verbatim "Change Gid.msg to be 16 bytes." (MERGED, clalancette). All three failed-condition quotes check out. element_retyped for field Gid.data follows S1's rule (declaration changed, element still present; definition_mismatch listed alongside). Condition 3 as `other` (unvalidated wire sequence length — an internal defect of the composition's deserializer) is per S1's treatment of internal defects. Loudness: silent_documented/run is right — the only messages are run-time deserialization errors that do not identify a type/definition mismatch; humble has no type-hash check at connection. Resolution: recommended is right — urfeex's working observation is a locally compiled Humble backport with a Rolling (not Jazzy) publisher, with the fix's output "sequence size exceeds remaining buffer" and "No memory footprint increase observable :-)"; per S1 a fix shown working with a different peer is recommended, and neither side's revision is identified; #828's later "the issue no longer occurs" states no versions.
